prompt: How much did volume move after February's price rises? For each price rise that took effect from 1 to 28 February 2025, give the percentage change in units from the before window to the after window: 100 times (units after minus units before) divided by units before, rounded to 1 decimal with ROUND. A rise with no units before shows a missing change. A price rise is a version in price_history whose list_price_eur is higher than that of the product's version before it, dated by its valid_from. Its change week is the week (Monday to Sunday) that holds valid_from. The before window is the 8 weeks just before the change week and the after window the 8 weeks just after it; the change week itself is in neither. Units come from weekly_units, which has a row for every product and week (week_start is the Monday), with 0 for a week with no sale. Leave out a change of a product whose launch_date is later than the first day of its before window (the Monday 8 weeks before the change week): it was not on sale for the whole window. Return three columns, in this order: product_id, valid_from and pct_change. Return one row for each price rise that stays. Any row order is fine.

output_contract.grain: one row per price rise from 1 to 28 February 2025 of a product on sale for its whole before window

hints: Next, write the percentage change from each rise's units before and after.
The base of the change is the before window, and a rise with nothing sold before has no base, so its change stays missing.
faded_shape:
WITH versions AS (
  -- one row per product and price version, with the list price of the version before it
  SELECT product_id, valid_from, list_price_eur,
    LAG(list_price_eur) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY valid_from) AS prev_price
  FROM price_history
), rises AS (
  -- one row per price rise from 1 to 28 February 2025 of a product on sale for its whole before window
  SELECT v.product_id, v.valid_from, CAST(date_trunc('week', v.valid_from) AS DATE) AS change_week
  FROM versions v
  JOIN products p ON p.product_id = v.product_id
  WHERE v.list_price_eur > v.prev_price
    AND v.valid_from BETWEEN DATE '2025-02-01' AND DATE '2025-02-28'
    AND p.launch_date <= CAST(date_trunc('week', v.valid_from) AS DATE) - INTERVAL 56 DAY
), windows AS (
  -- one row per price rise: its units before and after
  SELECT r.product_id, r.valid_from,
    SUM(CASE WHEN w.week_start < r.change_week THEN w.units ELSE 0 END) AS units_before,
    SUM(CASE WHEN w.week_start > r.change_week THEN w.units ELSE 0 END) AS units_after
  FROM rises r
  JOIN weekly_units w ON w.product_id = r.product_id
    AND w.week_start BETWEEN r.change_week - INTERVAL 56 DAY AND r.change_week + INTERVAL 56 DAY
  GROUP BY r.product_id, r.valid_from
)
SELECT product_id, valid_from,
why_this_works: The before window is the base of the change, and dropping products launched inside it keeps every base a full 8 weeks of sales.
